To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the induction of Foss protein in visual cortex is much stronger in young cats than adults, that the distribution of Fos protein is different between ages, that there is a transient component to the induction of FOS protein, and that the magnitude of induction is much stronger in visual than frontal cortex.
the inducibility, magnitude and laminar pattern of Fos protein expression are age-dependent in cat visual cortex.
Fos protein is induced in visual cortex of young kittens by brief periods of visual experience but not in adults and that the inducibility in visual cortex is greater in young kittens than in adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Fos protein as a possible mediator of synaptic plasticity in visual cortical circuits.
the molecular mechanisms that control the development and plasticity of the visual cortex.
understanding the molecular basis of plasticity in sensory cortex and its relation to the critical period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnitude of Fos protein induction in the cat visual cortex is age dependent, but the laminar distribution is not.
Fos protein is not a good indicator of neural activity level in cat visual cortex.
the induction of FOS protein is related to the level of plastic change in the visual cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inducibility and laminar distribution patterns of Fos in the visual cortex of adult cats are very different from those in young kittens, suggesting that Fos induction in visual cortex is not merely a reflection of neuronal activity but may be related to the level of plastic change in visual cortex during the critical period of development.
the Fos protein induction in visual cortex of the young kitten is greater than that in the adult cat, and that the induction pattern in the young kitten is different from that in the adult.
the induction of FOS protein in visual cortex of kittens is greater than in adult cats.
